text:
Nick Cousins scores the kind of goals that don't show up in highlight packages until they win games. With 2:18 left in a 2-2 game on Saturday, he got a stick on a Thomas Chabot shot that our model gave a 3 percent chance of going in, and it went in. Ottawa beat Utah 4-2, and by our win probability model that one deflection moved the Senators from 52 percent to 90.

On the run of play, this was a coin flip. The teams split 121 shot attempts almost evenly, and our numbers say Utah deserved to win 51 percent of the time. The Mammoth had the better first period, out-chancing Ottawa 1.21 to 0.63 in expected goals (the quality of chances), but went into the break tied after Clayton Keller answered Fabian Zetterlund's early power-play goal. Ottawa had the better third, 1.81 to 0.90, and that is where the game was settled.

The third was busy. Michael Amadio put Ottawa ahead at 6:29. Barrett Hayton tipped one in at 9:53 to tie it and swing Utah from 18 percent to 48. Samuel Ersson then made the save that mattered most, stopping Liam O'Brien on a 23 percent look late in the period, and about two minutes later Cousins found the deflection. Shane Pinto sealed it with 16 seconds left.

Ersson finished with 30 saves on 32 shots, a little better than expected, and got a star for it. Karel Vejmelka, coming off a rough stretch, allowed three on 20, slightly worse than the shots deserved. Keller was Utah's best player, a goal and an assist on six shots, but Logan Cooley, coming off his fifth career hat trick and the subject of most of the week's Utah headlines, was kept off the scoresheet.

For the Senators, this is a useful win for a team playing through injuries, with Warren Foegele and Andre Burakovsky out for weeks. It is also a reminder of how thin their margins are. They threw 40 hits, won the third, and needed a deflection off a point shot to get two points. Most nights a team gets about what it deserves. On this one Ottawa got a bit more, and we doubt it minds.
headline: Nick Cousins tips in a 3 percent winner
